statement: Defense obligations and EPA obligations are different orders of magnitude in the same fiscal year.
evidence: FY2025 obligations: Defense $1451.3B, EPA $34.3B, ratio 42 to 1. Both figures are agency obligations.
caveat: Obligations are commitments, not cash outlays. A ratio is not a proposal to move the money.

statement: Defense obligations exceed the combined obligations of USDA, EPA, HUD, and Interior.
evidence: FY2025: Defense $1451.3B against $444.3B for the four-agency group (3.3 to 1).
caveat: The four-agency group is an author grouping for this dashboard, not an official category. It leaves out Energy and Education on purpose so the group stays close to food, water, shelter, and land.

statement: HHS obligations are larger than Defense and are not treated as a livingry priority.
evidence: FY2025 HHS obligations $2794.3B, mostly Medicare and Medicaid.
caveat: Agency totals include mandatory spending. HHS is reported beside the group and never added into it.

statement: One contractor registration can be the same order of magnitude as a whole agency.
evidence: Largest Lockheed registration in the FY2025 top 15 (LOCKHEED MARTIN CORPORATION, UEI G4KDGE4JFFK7): $34.1B. EPA obligations the same year: $34.3B. Other Lockheed registrations in the top 15, not added: UEI XFJMYSYFJEK4 $10.4B, UEI H7PNSVNN5827 $6.1B.
caveat: A recipient's contract receipts and an agency's total obligations are different kinds of quantity. The comparison is scale, not a trade-off anyone voted on.

statement: High average food supply and a large food-insecurity shortfall coexist in the United States.
evidence: United States food supply 3947 kcal per person per day (2023); 10.3% moderate or severe food insecurity in 2023.
caveat: Coexistence is not a cause. The years may differ. The supply figure is an average and says nothing about distribution.

statement: Real GDP per person and the atmospheric CO2 stock rose over the same decades.
evidence: United States GDP per capita (constant 2015 dollars): $39,200 in 1990, $67,946 in 2025. Mauna Loa annual mean, full years only: 354.5 ppm in 1990, 427.3 ppm in 2025. Latest month: 427.55 ppm in 2026-08.
caveat: Shown side by side on purpose. They are not combined into an index, and neither causes the other by virtue of sharing a chart.

statement: Global undernourishment fell while the atmospheric CO2 stock rose.
evidence: World undernourishment 12.8% in 2000, 7.5% in 2019, before the projection footnote. FAO marks 2020-2025 as projections; 2025 is 7.8%. Mauna Loa full-year mean 354.5 ppm in 1990, 427.3 ppm in 2025.
caveat: This is the manuscript's own concession, not a rebuttal of it: a flow can improve while a stock deteriorates. FAO's whole undernourishment series is estimated, and years marked as projections are not used as the endpoint.

statement: FAO does not publish a United States undernourishment rate. It publishes a floor.
evidence: SDG 2.1.1 for the United States is '<2.5' in 2024, and the same floor in 24 years of this pull.
caveat: Below 2.5% is not a measurement of 2.5%, and it is not evidence that hunger is gone. The United States shortfall on this dashboard is SDG 2.1.2 food insecurity.

statement: Land required per 100g of protein differs by more than an order of magnitude across foods.
evidence: Highest in the table: Lamb & Mutton at 184.8 m2 per 100g protein. Lowest: Prawns (farmed) at 2.01 m2 (92 to 1). Beef herd 163.6 m2 against tofu 2.2 m2 (74 to 1).
caveat: Poore and Nemecek, Science, 2018, via Our World in Data. The grapher year is 2010. A published cross-section, not a live feed. Per protein, not per calorie. Farmed prawns sit at the bottom because the metric is land, which does not count the feed, water, and energy that metric leaves out.

statement: United States military expenditure is a few percent of GDP.
evidence: SIPRI via Our World in Data: 3.12% of GDP in 2025.
caveat: This is a share of GDP. It is not comparable to the USAspending obligation figures above, and the two are never placed in one ratio.
